title: Discarding regular centers in a finite surface blowup tower
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral excellent Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$ [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose $T_N\to\cdots\to T_0=S$ is a finite sequence of ordinary blowups at reduced closed points [def-nagata-global-blowup], each of local dimension $2$, with every $T_i$ normal. Then there is a finite sequence $Z_M\to\cdots\to Z_0=S$ of ordinary blowups at singular reduced closed points, with $M\leq N$, every $Z_j$ normal, and all centers of local dimension $2$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. There are open subschemes $V\subseteq Z_M$ and $W\subseteq T_N$ containing their respective singular loci, and an $S$-isomorphism $V\cong W$. The image in $S$ of every retained center is the image of some center in the given tower. The empty tower is allowed. This asserts no factorization of $Z_M$ through $T_N$.

source.place: Tag 0BBV, lemma-rational-to-gorenstein, phrase singular closed points: auxiliary pruning argument; Tag 0AGR, lemma-blowup-regular, and divisors.tex Tag 01OF, lemma-blowing-up, isomorphism away from the center. The generic pruning assertion is the agent-written expansion described in the report.

proof.text: First record the permanence facts needed for the construction. On any Noetherian stage the reduced structure on a closed point has a quasi-coherent ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; that ideal is of finite type since every ideal in an affine Noetherian coordinate ring is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Hence each point blowup is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], in particular of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and its source is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Each stage is integral by [lem-per-integral-blowup-projective-geometry]: the center ideal is nonzero because a center of local dimension $2$ is not the generic point. Finally, choose a finite affine cover by excellent rings on the preceding stage. The definition of finite type gives a finite affine cover upstairs by finite-type algebras over those rings [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. They are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]. Thus all the given $T_i$, and all stages constructed below, have finite affine covers by excellent rings. These arguments apply anew at each blowup and require no ample line bundle.

For every stage considered, its regular locus is open: on each excellent affine chart the J-2 clause of [def-exc-excellent-ring], applied to the coordinate ring as an algebra over itself, says precisely that its regular-local-ring locus is open. These loci agree on overlaps because the local rings are the same, and their union is the regular locus [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Write $\operatorname{Sing}(X)$ for the complementary closed subset. An isomorphism between open subschemes identifies their local rings, hence identifies the singular points lying in those opens. No assertion about finiteness of the singular locus or the global dimension of later stages is needed here.

source.place: definition-excellent and the following paragraph (closed singular set); agent expansion of Tag 0BBV

proof.text: Induct on the number $i$ of processed arrows of the given tower. Keep a tower $Z_{m(i)}\to\cdots\to Z_0=S$ with $m(i)\leq i$, only singular reduced closed centers of local dimension $2$, normal stages, and opens $V_i\subseteq Z_{m(i)}$, $W_i\subseteq T_i$ containing their entire singular loci, with an $S$-isomorphism $\phi_i:V_i\xrightarrow{\sim}W_i$. Also keep the record that each retained center has the same image in $S$ as one of the first $i$ given centers. For $i=0$, take $m(0)=0$, $V_0=W_0=S$, and $\phi_0=\mathrm{id}_S$. This establishes every invariant, including the assertion for the empty tower.

Let $b:T_{i+1}\to T_i$ have center $p$. Suppose first that $p$ is regular. The open $R=(T_i)_{\rm reg}$ contains $p$, is integral by restriction of the integral-scheme definition [def-pc-integral-scheme], and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Its local ring at $p$ still has dimension $2$. Apply [lem-per-regular-point-blowup-acyclic] to $R$ and $p$: its blowup is regular. The flat-base-change isomorphism [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], with the comparison specified by [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map], identifies this blowup with $b^{-1}(R)$; an open inclusion is flat since its local homomorphisms are isomorphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus every point above $p$ is regular. Away from $p$, [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies local rings. Consequently every singular point of $T_{i+1}$ lies above $\operatorname{Sing}(T_i)\subseteq W_i\setminus\{p\}$. Discard this arrow: set $m(i+1)=m(i)$, replace $V_i$ by $\phi_i^{-1}(W_i\setminus\{p\})$, and set $W_{i+1}=b^{-1}(W_i\setminus\{p\})$. The restricted $\phi_i$ and the inverse of $b$ give the required $S$-isomorphism. The removed points in $V_i$ were regular, so the new open still contains all singular points of the unchanged $Z_{m(i)}$. All other invariants are unchanged.

proof.text: Suppose instead that $p$ is singular. Then $p\in W_i$; put $q=\phi_i^{-1}(p)$. Its local ring is isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{T_i,p}$, so $q$ is singular and has local dimension $2$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Crucially $q$ is closed in the whole scheme $Z_{m(i)}$, not just in $V_i$: its closure lies in the closed singular locus from Step 2, hence in $V_i$; but $q$ is closed in $V_i$ since $p$ is closed in $W_i$. Thus that closure equals $\{q\}$. Give $q$ its reduced induced closed structure. By the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], $\phi_i$ identifies this center on $V_i$ with the given reduced center $p$ on $W_i$. Retain a step by forming $c:Z_{m(i)+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_q Z_{m(i)}\to Z_{m(i)}$. Step 1 applies, so this stage is integral and Noetherian and has excellent affine charts. Set $m(i+1)=m(i)+1$.

source.place: Tag 0BBV (lemma-rational-to-gorenstein), singular-closed-point requirement; agent-written closedness argument using the closed singular locus

proof.text: In this retained case, set $V_{i+1}=c^{-1}(V_i)$ and $W_{i+1}=b^{-1}(W_i)$. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] and [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] to the two open inclusions (flat on the identical local rings [def-weil-flat-morphism]) and to the isomorphism $\phi_i$. Since their reduced center ideals correspond, these comparisons give an isomorphism $V_{i+1}\cong W_{i+1}$ over $\phi_i$, hence over $S$. Each point outside $W_{i+1}$ maps outside $W_i$ and is away from $p$; the complement isomorphism [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies its local ring with a regular local ring of $T_i$. The identical argument for $c$ shows that every point outside $V_{i+1}$ is regular. Thus the new opens contain the entire singular loci. Finally $Z_{m(i)+1}$ is normal: on $V_{i+1}$ its local rings are those of the normal $T_{i+1}$, and outside it $c$ is an isomorphism onto points of the normal $Z_{m(i)}$. This is normality directly from [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], without assuming that blowups of arbitrary normal surfaces stay normal.

proof.text: For a retained arrow, $\phi_i$ is an $S$-isomorphism and sends $q$ to the given center $p$, so these centers have the same image in $S$. This extends the image record and completes the inductive step in both cases. At $i=N$ put $M=m(N)$, $V=V_N$, $W=W_N$. Each processed arrow increased $m$ by zero or one, so $M\leq N$; the invariant gives normality, singular reduced closed centers of local dimension $2$, and the desired $S$-isomorphism of opens containing both singular loci. If every arrow was discarded then $M=0$, and if $N=0$ the base case applies. The construction only uses isomorphisms on these opens and does not assert a morphism $Z_M\to T_N$.

split_report.summary: Proved the pruning statement by an explicit induction on the input arrows. At a regular center use regularity of the blowup of the regular open; at a singular center transport the center across the maintained open isomorphism, prove its global closedness, and compare the two blowups. Normality is checked locally, never inferred from a general normal-blowup assertion. Reused all required facts from existing nodes; created no new nodes. Statement unchanged.
